canonical_bindings.use: Keeps product-capability, system, evidence, and residue claims distinct.
Keeps canonical meaning distinct from projected presentation.
Keeps the Workspace coordination identity distinct from the capability, repository, and runtime.
Requires exact semantic and generated-system predecessors before implementation claims.
Defines what the parent CyberAlchemy product must enable independently of a particular UI or runtime.

proposals.normative_voice: CyberAlchemy Workspace is the inspect-only Product Capability through which a person navigates source-owned definitions, products, projects, and ontologies, examines their identity, status, meaning, provenance, ownership, boundary, claim ceiling, and source epoch, and enters a Project-specific surface without transferring semantic or authority ownership to the interface.
proposals.plain_language_voice: The Workspace is the front door for seeing what CyberAlchemy contains, what each thing means, who owns it, and where to go next.
proposals.domain_context_voice: The parent CyberAlchemy product owns the capability. The Workspace Project coordinates construction. Source packages retain meaning and authority.
proposals.owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 product owner plus CyberAlchemy Workspace Project owner
proposals.forbidden_collapse: CyberAlchemy Workspace is not a CAV2-D60 Project, repository browser, definition registry, ontology runtime, product catalog authority, or owner of Essays.

proposals.normative_voice: A Workspace Snapshot is an immutable, version-identified projection of registered definitions, products, projects, and ontologies at one exact source epoch, preserving each record's source-owned posture and claim ceiling.
proposals.plain_language_voice: A snapshot says exactly which version of CyberAlchemy meaning the screen is showing.
proposals.domain_context_voice: The runtime may generate and display a snapshot but cannot use it to change or promote its sources.
proposals.forbidden_collapse: A Workspace Snapshot is not a registry, source of truth, acceptance decision, or proof of currentness beyond its bound epoch.

proposals.normative_voice: A Workspace Record is one projected semantic record whose collection kind, stable identity, label, status, meaning, owner route, provenance, boundary, claim ceiling, and source epoch remain inspectable and non-collapsible.
proposals.plain_language_voice: A Workspace Record is a faithful read-only card for one definition, product, project, or ontology.
proposals.domain_context_voice: The projection is presentation data derived from source-owned records.
proposals.owner_route: CyberAlchemy Workspace Product Capability owner plus projected source owner
proposals.forbidden_collapse: A Workspace Record is not the semantic source it projects and cannot accept, edit, or promote that source.

proposals.normative_voice: A Project Entry is a Workspace Record for one CAV2-D60 Project that preserves the Project's stable identity and owner route and may identify a separate Project-specific surface without making navigation an ownership transfer.
proposals.plain_language_voice: A Project Entry lets someone open a project such as Essays while keeping that project in charge of its own meaning and work.
proposals.domain_context_voice: Essays is the first projected Project Entry and retains its own product, capability, and runtime boundaries.
proposals.owner_route: Projected Project owner plus CyberAlchemy Workspace Product Capability owner
proposals.forbidden_collapse: Opening a Project Entry is not adopting, activating, editing, or transferring ownership of the Project.
